sam: Heads-up — saw a reproducible TP slowdown on nightly that looks like all-reduce saturation when messages are small (<= 64KB). ring > tree in terms of tail latency.
maya: can you paste the perf numbers? is this with the latest kvcache micro-batching change?
sam: yes, landed the kvcache micro-batch split that reduces per-request peak mem but creates many ~16-48KB tensors during KV sync. Quick numbers from a deterministic run (4x A100, TP=2):
```
baseline (no split): avg step 7.8ms, p99 12.1ms
with split (many small msgs): avg step 9.5ms, p99 24.8ms
force NCCL_TREE=1: avg 8.9ms, p99 13.7ms
```
lee: interesting. so tree helped p99 a lot. did you try toggling `NCCL_BUFFSIZE`/chunking or overlap flags?
sam: tried `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152` (2MB) — little change. But enabling larger internal chunking helped only for larger msg sizes. The core issue seems to be per-call overhead + serialization fragmentation.
tj: do we have traces? can we check nvprof / nccl trace to see if many small launches are serialized on the ring causing head-of-line?
sam: uploaded an nsys capture and NCCL TRACE. Key pattern: with ring, we see many tiny `allreduce` ops back-to-back with short gaps; tree aggregates slightly better and reduces cross-device handshake overhead. Attaching snippet:```
[NSYS]  kernel    start(us)   duration(us)
allreduce_k1   1000   120
allreduce_k2   1200   110
... many 80-120us kernels, host syncs in between
```
perf-bot: autotest run 1819023000 completed — regression flagged for tp/inference-kv-split on p99 latency (+2.1x).
maya: hypothesis: kvcache micro-batch strategy reduces single op size but increases op count so ring's O(n) handshake cost dominates. tree's log(n) connectivity amortizes it. Also if message size falls below NCCL internals' threshold, ring uses slower path.
lee: action items: (1) add a config toggle to prefer tree for small-message workloads; (2) instrument our runtime to report "allreduce msg size distribution" in the trace export; (3) run ablation where we coalesce KV deltas on the host to test reduced op count.
tj: for (1) we can set NCCL_ALGO=tree or force topology in the runtime selection. For (2) I'll add a small telemetry event with histogram buckets: <4KB, 4-16KB,16-64KB,64KB+.
sam: also add a test against simulated network jitter to ensure fallback doesn't regress throughput. If tree has other regressions for big msgs, we need an auto-policy: use tree when >X% of allreduces are <Y KB.
maya: agreed. small PR to runtime: policy engine that picks NCCL algorithm based on median msg size + historical p99. I'll draft.
lee: can we add a short repro script? something like:
```
# repro script outline
PYTHONPATH=./python pytest tests/perf/test_tp_allreduce.py::test_kv_split_repro --runs 50
# toggles: NCCL_ALGO=ring|tree, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=..., REDWOOD_KV_SPLIT=1
```
sam: great — I'll attach nsys capture + raw logs to the perf ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
